subject: Messaging + proof points for Standard Demo v1 (benchmark substantiation + public-safe wording)

body:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Aug 6, 2024 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Messaging + proof points for Standard Demo v1 (benchmark substantiation + public-safe wording)

Team — quick escalation before we lock Demo Deck v1.

I’m seeing a few benchmark-style claims in the working deck + speaker notes that need substantiation *and* tightened wording so they’re safe to use live (and in any follow-up recap email). Specifically:

1) “2x faster” / “sub-300ms p95” style latency statements
2) “30–50% cheaper” / “lower $/1K tokens” type cost statements
3) Reliability claims (fallback keeps apps online, etc.)

Asks:
- Please point me to the source of truth for what ranges we can safely say (and what’s strictly internal-only).
- Recommend final wording that’s accurate, non-absolute, and doesn’t read like a public benchmark vs a named competitor.
- Confirm if we should keep *all* numbers out of the deck and reserve the “ranges” to spoken talk track only.

If helpful: my bias is to keep slide copy qualitative and put numbers only in an appendix slide we can omit, but I want alignment w/ Sales.

Can you send back proposed wording + citations/notes by EOD?

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes
VP Marketing, Redwood Inference


---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Aug 6, 2024 at 12:03 PM
Subject: Re: Messaging + proof points for Standard Demo v1 (benchmark substantiation + public-safe wording)

Yep — agree we should tighten.

Source of truth: “Benchmark Proof Points - Slides Inputs” (Drive) — it’s the table we’ve been using to keep claims within validated ranges.

Proposal (public-safe / live-demo safe):

A) Latency:
- Slide wording (no numbers): “Consistently low latency with streaming + production routing controls.”
- Spoken option (if asked): “In internal tests on comparable hardware and fixed prompts, we typically see meaningful p95 improvements from batching/caching and kernel selection. Results vary by model, context length, and traffic shape.”

B) Cost:
- Slide wording: “Lower unit cost via batching, caching, and quantization profiles — with visibility into the tradeoffs.”
- Spoken option (if asked): “Teams often find double-digit % reductions in cost-per-output after tuning batching/caching and selecting an appropriate quantization profile. We can measure this in your workload.”

C) Reliability:
- Slide wording: “Graceful degradation: routing + automatic fallback policies.”
- Spoken option: “If a route hits a latency/error threshold, policies can fail over to a compatible variant/region to keep the app online.”

I can update the talk track to gate any numeric statement behind an ‘if asked’ sidebar. If you want, I’ll remove the remaining hard numbers from the slides today.

Sharing links:
- Benchmark Proof Points - Slides Inputs (Drive)
- Deck - Redwood Standard Demo (Working)

Soojin

Attachment: Benchmark Proof Points - Slides Inputs (Google Sheet link)
Attachment: Deck - Redwood Standard Demo (Working).pptx (Drive link)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Aug 6, 2024 at 1:21 PM
Subject: Re: Messaging + proof points for Standard Demo v1 (benchmark substantiation + public-safe wording)

+1 to removing hard numbers from the slides.

One request from the field: we need *something* punchy for the first 5 mins. If we can’t say “30–50% cheaper,” what’s the strongest approved line we can use verbally?

AEs keep getting pressed on “how much cheaper/faster” even in the first call.

Stephanie

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Aug 6, 2024 at 2:04 PM
Subject: Re: Messaging + proof points for Standard Demo v1 (benchmark substantiation + public-safe wording)

Agree with direction:
- No hard numbers on standard deck slides.
- Numbers only in (1) internal enablement materials and (2) “if asked” talk track, tied to “internal tests / results vary.”

We should avoid anything that reads like a public benchmark or a guarantee.

If Sales needs a punchy line: anchor on “measurable improvements” + “we’ll validate on your traffic” rather than a number.

Jordan

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Aug 6, 2024 at 3:37 PM
Subject: Re: Messaging + proof points for Standard Demo v1 (benchmark substantiation + public-safe wording)

Thanks — this is the right structure.

Stephanie: I hear you. Let’s define a *single* verbally-safe “punchy” line that doesn’t imply a guarantee.

Soojin — can you propose a one-liner we can all live with, plus the exact disclaimer sentence right after it?

Also: please scrub any explicit values (e.g., “sub-300ms”) from screenshots/console panels if they sneak into slide captures.

Camila


---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Aug 7, 2024 at 10:18 AM
Subject: Re: Messaging + proof points for Standard Demo v1 (benchmark substantiation + public-safe wording)

Proposed “punchy but safe” verbal line (intro section):

One-liner:
“Redwood gives you predictable, measurable improvements in latency and unit cost by making batching, caching, quantization, and routing policies easy to tune and observe.”

Follow-on disclaimer sentence (immediately after):
“The exact lift depends on model choice, context length, and traffic shape — we’ll validate with your prompts and constraints during eval.”

If pressed for a number:
“We often see double-digit percentage gains after tuning, and we can show the before/after in the console on your workload.”

I’ll update speaker notes to include those exact lines and remove any remaining numeric claims from the deck.

Soojin

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Aug 7, 2024 at 4:28 PM
Subject: Re: Messaging + proof points for Standard Demo v1 (benchmark substantiation + public-safe wording)

Approved.

Final guidance for Demo Deck v1 / talk track:
- Slides: qualitative only (no “2x”, no “$ / 1K tokens”, no p95 numbers).
- Talk track: use Soojin’s one-liner + disclaimer verbatim.
- If asked for quantification: “often double-digit % gains after tuning” is the ceiling of what we should say without pulling up a customer-specific measurement.
- Never frame as a public benchmark vs a named competitor. If a prospect brings up a vendor by name, we pivot to “we can run side-by-side on your prompts during eval.”

Soojin — please sync these changes into the working deck + the speaker notes doc today. Stephanie — I’ll send a short field note for the enablement email with the exact approved phrasing.

Camila

Camila Reyes
VP Marketing, Redwood Inference
